chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from 'Ali ibn Isma'il, from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, from his paternal uncle, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام and said: May I be made your ransom, a man's khuff may be torn, so he puts his hand inside it and wipes the top of his feet—does that suffice him? He said: “Yes.”

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam Mūsā al-Kāẓim عليه السلام, the Imam being asked for the ruling
key_terms.أَيُجْزِيهِ: does it suffice him; is it legally valid
key_terms.ظَهْرَ قَدَمَيْهِ: the upper part of his two feet

ai.seo_question: Does wiping the top of the feet through a torn khuff suffice in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about wudu (ablution), specifically wiping the feet when footwear is torn. Imam Mūsā عليه السلام states that if a person can insert his hand and wipe the upper part of his feet, that is sufficient.
